slides.title: You're not a [small version] of a big firm.
slides.lede: A boutique's edge usually comes from focus, senior attention, speed of judgment and sector understanding. Five moves to make a rebrand turn that into a clearer client choice.

slides.title: Rebrand for a [business reason], not a style preference.
slides.note: Ask partners separately to describe the ideal client and differentiator. If the answers differ materially, the problem is **probably strategic**.

slides.title: Position around [client problems], not practice labels.

cards.label: Client problem
cards.text: Helping founder-led technology companies manage sensitive people issues without slowing growth.

slides.title: Keep [star partners] inside one firm system.
slides.text: Don't hide strong partner reputations. Place them inside a consistent firm system, so succession is easier and recruits see a platform bigger than any one name.

slides.title: Test the identity in [real contexts], not on a logo sheet.

items.title: Pitch document
items.text: A high-value proposal, not a mock-up.

items.title: Recruitment page
items.text: As a lateral hire would see it.

slides.title: Inventory every touchpoint, then measure [business outcomes], not applause.
slides.text: Old bios, directory entries and signatures left in circulation signal uncertainty. Set baselines first, then track qualified enquiries, proposal win rate and referrer feedback.

slides.title: An asset, not an expensive announcement.
